image_normalization: Per-volume 1st/99th percentiles of intensity-thresholded largest connected cranial foreground; no cohort-fitted preprocessing.
orientation: Canonical RAS then orthogonal 1.5 mm isotropic RAS resampling; axial neurological display.
cranial_foreground: Largest connected component above 8% of 98th percentile of positive intensities. Longest axial run with area at least 35% of maximum; nine fixed 45–85% fractions of cranial extent. This heuristic is not validated brain segmentation.
resize: Fixed per-volume xy crop with 6 mm margin; preserve aspect ratio with black square padding, resize 224 bilinear, repeat grayscale RGB.
selection_policy: Besga provider groups ea=AD,crl=CN; tb bipolar excluded. Deterministic subject-stratified 60/20/20 using seed 1729; OpenNeuro entire cohort external. No forced dementia-severity mapping.
clinical_metadata_policy: Age and source sex/gender retained locally for subgroup descriptions only, not image model inputs. Besga gender coding not inferred. Original NIfTI headers and private biomarker tables are not exported.
evaluation_policy: Only Besga validation may guide auxiliary model selection. Besga test and all OpenNeuro labels are excluded from selection. MCI may be predicted but excluded from binary AD/CN scoring.
limitations: Exploratory preprocessing only; visual review is gross QC, not validated anatomical or clinical quality assurance.
No atlas registration, validated skull stripping, bias-field correction, scanner harmonization or clinical validation.
Preprocessing failures stop the pipeline rather than silently dropping cases.
Small single-source Besga development sample and only one OpenNeuro AD case; no robust external validation claim.
Source/cohort overlap and patient-identity deduplication beyond exact image pixels remain unresolved.
No model training or label harmonization to the existing severity task performed.
Visible intercohort intensity differences and within-cohort head-pitch/sharpness variation remain; the sampling rule does not provide anatomically registered slices.

visual_qc.reviewer: Codex gross visual QC; no radiologist review
visual_qc.label_policy: Final sheets show only source subject IDs and slice fraction. Representative full grids selected by subject-ID order, independent of diagnosis.
findings: All reviewed central images contain recognizable axial brain anatomy; no blank image, gross orientation failure, or obvious brain clipping in inspected sheets.
Six representative nine-slice grids show progression from inferior temporal/brainstem levels through ventricular and upper cerebral levels.
Source head pitch and axial anatomy differ across participants; no atlas registration was performed.
OpenNeuro scans generally have darker brain intensities relative to extracranial tissue than Besga; no scanner harmonization was performed.
Variable sharpness remains; no subject was excluded based on visual appearance.
visual_qc.scope: Gross image rendering and anatomical plausibility only; not clinical or validated anatomical quality assurance.

protocol_history.reason_changed: Gross visual anatomical QC showed excess inferior cerebellum/neck slices; initial sheets displayed source diagnoses but no model predictions or outcomes were inspected.

protocol_history.qa_labels: Subject IDs and slice fraction only; no diagnoses or model outcomes.
protocol_history.png_policy: Every manifest PNG regenerated; superseded QA sheets removed.
